title: PR labeling + release note capture notes (model metadata + changelog generator)
content:
Purpose
- Working notes for how we capture structured release-note info at PR time, so the changelog generator can produce consistent customer-visible notes + internal audit notes.
- This doc is intentionally practical: label names, required fields, validation rules, and examples of good/bad entries.

Context / why this exists
- Today release notes are inconsistent: sometimes missing, sometimes too vague (“misc fixes”), sometimes include internal-only details.
- The new pipeline will generate release notes from model metadata + change events. We still need a reliable way to annotate code changes that affect metadata/events/templates/console/docs.
- Decision direction (see ADR-0143): hybrid approach.
  - Source of truth for “what changed” is registry/control-plane event stream.
  - PR labels + a small structured “release note entry” field provide editorial intent + category/severity and links.

Scope of this PR-labeling doc
- Applies to repos that can change customer-visible model behavior or release-note output:
  - redwood-model-registry
  - redwood (control plane)
  - redwood-docs
  - sdk repos (python/typescript) when endpoint shape changes
- Applies to PRs that:
  - change model metadata schema, records, migrations
  - change event schema / event emission
  - change changelog generator templates/category mapping
  - change Console release notes surfaces (RBAC/redaction especially)
  - change public docs release notes generation

Non-goals
- This is not the final editorial style guide (see Confluence: customer-release-notes-taxonomy-and-style-guide).
- This does not replace the model-level metadata fields (public/internal notes) — it complements them.


1) Required labels (exact strings)
We’re standardizing on a small set of required labels. CI will enforce: (a) at least one category label, (b) one audience label, and (c) if applicable, a severity label.

1.1 Category labels (choose 1+, required)
- rn:breaking
  - Meaning: a customer may need to change code/config/prompting, or an API/contract changed.
  - Example triggers: removing a model alias, changing default sampling behavior for a pinned alias, changing schema/field names in public API.
- rn:deprecation
  - Meaning: introducing or advancing a deprecation timeline. Must include “effective date” and “what to do next”.
- rn:security
  - Meaning: security-relevant change. Often limited details publicly. Requires Security reviewer ack.
- rn:quality
  - Meaning: output quality changed (better or worse), as measured by evals/guardrails. Must avoid overstating; include evidence link internally.
- rn:performance
  - Meaning: latency/throughput/cost characteristics changed.
- rn:bugfix
  - Meaning: fixes incorrect behavior (including incorrect release note generation, RBAC leaks, etc.).
- rn:docs
  - Meaning: docs-only customer-facing changes.
- rn:internal
  - Meaning: no customer-visible release note entry required (still logged internally). CI will allow skipping public entry if audience label is internal-only.

Notes
- Use rn:internal sparingly. If the PR affects model behavior, schema, or rollout semantics, it is not internal.
- If multiple categories apply, list all, but keep the release note entry concise and pick one “primary category” in the release note form (below).

1.2 Audience labels (choose 1, required)
- rn:audience-public
  - Will show on docs-site + Console release notes.
- rn:audience-console-only
  - Intended for Console release notes but not the public docs feed (rare; requires PM + Docs ok).
- rn:audience-private
  - For Private upgrade bundles / offline exports. Typically includes more operational guidance.
- rn:audience-internal
  - Only visible to Redwood staff (audit/change log). Must not leak into customer surfaces.

1.3 Severity labels (optional but required for breaking/security)
- rn:sev-high
- rn:sev-med
- rn:sev-low

Rules
- rn:breaking => must include a severity label.
- rn:security => must include a severity label (public text likely minimal).
- rn:deprecation => severity optional but recommended.

1.4 Rollout-related labels (optional)
- rn:rollout-canary
- rn:rollout-ab
- rn:rollout-fallback

These do not drive customer-facing text directly; they help Console filtering and internal audit queries.


2) Required “Release note entry” fields (PR template)
Add the following block to the PR description (or required PR form fields where supported). CI will parse these fields.

2.1 Template (copy/paste)
Release note entry (required unless rn:audience-internal AND rn:internal):
- Primary category: [breaking|deprecation|security|quality|performance|bugfix|docs|internal]
- Customer impact: [one sentence]
- What changed: [1–2 sentences]
- Action required: [none|recommended|required] + [if recommended/required, what should customer do]
- Affected surfaces: [hosted|dedicated|private|sdk|console|docs] (comma-separated)
- Rollback/fallback: [none|supported] + [short guidance or link]
- References: [links to metadata version(s), event schema, docs page, eval run, incident, etc.]
- Public text (if different): [optional, only needed if we need to redact internal details]
- Internal-only notes: [optional; never shown to customers]

2.2 Field rules / validation
- “Customer impact” must be customer-readable (no internal acronyms without expansion).
- “What changed” should not include:
  - hostnames, internal ticket numbers that reveal customer names, raw prompts or customer data
  - precise exploit details for security fixes
- “References” MUST include at least one durable pointer:
  - model id + version (preferred) OR
  - schema version/hash OR
  - event type + version OR
  - docs URL (for docs-only)
- “Public text” is required if any of these labels are present:
  - rn:security
  - rn:audience-public AND PR contains internal-only operational details (common for infra changes)


3) Mapping labels/fields to changelog generator output
The generator will produce two streams:
- Public release notes (docs + Console): derived from “Public text” if provided; else from “Customer impact” + “What changed” after redaction checks.
- Internal change log (audit/support): includes “Internal-only notes”, exact PR SHA, author, reviewers, and any internal references.

Categorization
- PR “Primary category” drives the release note category bucket.
- Additional rn:* category labels become tags on the entry.

Severity handling
- Severity is shown in Console UI for admins and internal users; public docs will show “Important/Recommended/Info” wording based on severity + action required.
  - high + required => “Important”
  - med + recommended => “Recommended”
  - low + none => “Info”


4) Redaction + safe wording notes (quick checklist)
Before merging:
- Is there anything in “What changed” that reveals internal infrastructure specifics? (e.g., region capacity constraints, specific GPU vendor issues) If yes, move to internal-only notes.
- If referencing quality/evals:
  - Do not claim “improves accuracy by X%” unless we have a stable, customer-relevant metric and significance.
  - Use: “Quality: updated post-training snapshot; see evaluation summary.” Keep numbers internal unless approved.
- Security:
  - Public text should be minimal: “Security hardening for model metadata update pipeline.”
  - Internal notes should contain CVE/internal tracking and mitigation details.


5) Examples
5.1 Good example — performance improvement (public)
Labels:
- rn:performance
- rn:audience-public
- rn:sev-low

Release note entry:
- Primary category: performance
- Customer impact: Some requests may see lower time-to-first-token for long prompts under load.
- What changed: Improved continuous batching heuristics in the inference runtime used by the Hosted API for supported decoder-only models.
- Action required: none
- Affected surfaces: hosted
- Rollback/fallback: supported + “If you observe regressions, pin to prior model version or contact support; see rollback docs: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/rollbacks (placeholder)”
- References: model family: rw-llama-3.x, rollout policy: default-hosted, PR: <link>

Why it’s good
- States impact without promising universal improvement.
- Mentions scope (“Hosted API”, “supported models”).
- Provides rollback guidance.

5.2 Good example — deprecation (public + private)
Labels:
- rn:deprecation
- rn:audience-public
- rn:audience-private
- rn:sev-med

Release note entry:
- Primary category: deprecation
- Customer impact: A legacy model alias will be removed on 2025-12-01.
- What changed: Deprecated alias “rw-mistral-7b” in favor of “rw-mistral-7b-v2”. The legacy alias will stop receiving updates immediately and will be removed on 2025-12-01.
- Action required: required + Update your integration to use “rw-mistral-7b-v2” or pin a specific version.
- Affected surfaces: hosted, dedicated, private, sdk
- Rollback/fallback: supported + “Pin to a versioned model id before the removal date; Private customers can remain on prior bundle until next maintenance window.”
- References: model-id: rw-mistral-7b, new model-id: rw-mistral-7b-v2, docs: <link>

Why it’s good
- Gives a date.
- Clear required action.
- Covers Private nuance.

5.3 Good example — security fix (public minimal, internal detailed)
Labels:
- rn:security
- rn:audience-public
- rn:sev-high

Release note entry:
- Primary category: security
- Customer impact: Security hardening for model metadata change processing.
- What changed: [leave minimal]
- Action required: none
- Affected surfaces: hosted, console
- Rollback/fallback: none
- References: PR link
- Public text (if different): Security hardening for model metadata change processing.
- Internal-only notes: Fixed an authorization edge case in changelog preview artifacts that could expose internal-only notes in CI logs under misconfigured permissions. Reviewed with Security (Marcus Lin). Incident correlation: none.

Why it’s good
- Public text is appropriately vague.
- Internal notes contain the real details for audit.

5.4 Bad example — too vague
Labels:
- rn:bugfix
- rn:audience-public

Release note entry:
- Customer impact: Fixes stuff.
- What changed: Various improvements.

What’s wrong
- Not actionable, not searchable.
- Fails CI (missing required fields, no surfaces, no references).

5.5 Bad example — leaks internal info
Release note entry:
- What changed: “We had to revert the H100 kernel rollout in us-east-1 because of driver 535.129.03 issues causing OOMs.”

What’s wrong
- Region + hardware + driver version should be internal.
- Public wording should be: “Adjusted kernel selection to improve stability under some workloads.” Internal notes can keep the exact details.

5.6 Bad example — overstates quality
Release note entry:
- Customer impact: “Quality improved by 12%.”

What’s wrong
- 12% of what? Not necessarily customer-relevant; may not be statistically sound.
- Better: “Quality: updated snapshot with improved instruction following on internal eval set; see evaluation summary.” Numbers only with explicit approval and clear metric definition.


6) Edge cases / FAQs
Q: When can I skip a release note entry?
- Only when rn:audience-internal AND rn:internal AND the change doesn’t affect customer-visible behavior. CI will enforce this and require an explicit “Reason for skip” line:
  - Skip reason: [e.g., refactor/no behavior change]

Q: What about docs-only PRs?
- Use rn:docs + rn:audience-public. Release note entry still required but can be short; references should include the docs URL.

Q: PR spans multiple repos (e.g., registry + docs). Do I need two entries?
- One per PR. If the change is coordinated across PRs, each PR should contain its own entry and reference the “tracking PR”/Linear epic.

Q: How do we handle customer-specific notes?
- Do not put customer names in public text. Use rn:audience-private or rn:audience-internal as appropriate and coordinate with CS.


7) Action items / next steps
- [Connor] Add PR template block to redwood-model-registry + redwood repos (target by end of week; track under ENG-9826).
- [Sahana] Add CI parser + required checks (labels + required fields). Fail on missing “References”.
- [Wei] Confirm public wording patterns for severity mapping (Important/Recommended/Info) aligns with style guide.
- [Marissa/Jada] Confirm category label list matches the Console filters and taxonomy.
- [Michael] Confirm generator can ingest PR metadata for internal notes and attach to event-derived release note entries.

Changelog of this doc
- 2025-10-04: Initial draft.
- 2025-10-09: Added redaction rules + security example after RBAC leak hotfix discussion.
- 2025-10-11: Added audience labels and skip conditions to align with CI enforcement plan.
